evidence.detail: The exact v308 rs/Client class extends rs/C directly, making rs/C the application/game-shell base rather than a feature helper.

rs/C extends java.applet.Applet, implements Runnable plus component/focus/key/mouse/mouse-motion/mouse-wheel/window listeners, owns the frame/graphics/input state, runs the client loop and implements start/stop/destroy/update/paint lifecycle methods.
Classic RSApplet has the same Applet + Runnable + input/window listener role, owns the client frame/graphics shell and provides the game-loop/lifecycle surface inherited by Client.

proposals.note: RSApplet is a non-canonical semantic recovery name grounded in exact v308 behavior; classic client source is corroborating lineage evidence only.

evidence.detail: rs/E extends JFrame and stores exactly one rs/C applet reference. Its sized constructor creates the visible top-level Jagex window around that applet.
The frame delegates update(Graphics) and paint(Graphics) into its rs/C applet after the JFrame superclass call and routes cursor handling through the desktop window.
Classic RSFrame is the paired desktop-frame wrapper around RSApplet. v308 uses Swing JFrame rather than the older AWT Frame but preserves the same applet/window ownership role.
